title: EVD and shunt malfunction or infection
subtitle: Blocked, overdraining or infected CSF devices

sources.title: The insertion and management of external ventricular drains: an evidence-based consensus statement (Fried et al, Neurocrit Care 2016;24:61-81)
2017 Clinical practice guidelines for healthcare-associated ventriculitis and meningitis (Tunkel et al, Clin Infect Dis 2017;64:e34-e65)

sources.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
sources.title: Head injury: assessment and early management (NG232)

red_flags.text: Shunted patient with headache, vomiting and drowsiness: shunt failure until proven otherwise, even with a normal-looking scan.
Falling GCS, upward gaze palsy or bradycardia in a patient with a shunt or EVD.
EVD that has stopped draining, or a CSF column that no longer swings with pulse and respiration.
Sudden large volume of CSF from an EVD after moving or sitting the patient up: overdrainage, with a risk of subdural or remote haemorrhage.
Fever, wound erythema, CSF leak, or cloudy CSF in a patient with a device.
Abdominal pain, peritonitis or a pseudocyst in a patient with a ventriculoperitoneal shunt.

do_now.text: Airway, breathing and circulation. A patient with acute shunt failure can deteriorate within hours to herniation.
Call neurosurgery immediately. Only the neurosurgical team taps a shunt or manipulates an EVD.
EVD: check it is open, levelled to the prescribed reference point, unkinked, and the drip chamber at the prescribed height.
Clamp the EVD before moving, sitting up or transferring the patient, and reopen and re-level afterwards.

assess.text: GCS, pupils and eye movements, compared with the documented baseline.
Shunt: palpate along the tract for swelling, tenderness, erythema or a fluid collection. Note the valve type and any programmable setting.
EVD: record hourly output, CSF colour, the column swing, the zero reference and the drain height.
Ask about recent shunt surgery, previous failures and how this episode compares; parents and patients often recognise their own pattern.

investigate.text: CT head compared with the previous baseline scan: ventricular size, catheter position, haemorrhage, subdural collections.
Shunt series X-ray for disconnection, fracture or migration of the tubing.
CSF from the EVD or a neurosurgical shunt tap for cell count, glucose, protein, Gram stain and culture before antibiotics where it does not delay treatment.
Blood cultures, inflammatory markers, and abdominal imaging for peritoneal complications of a VP shunt.

resuscitate.text: Suspected device infection: send cultures, then start empirical intravenous antibiotics: a glycopeptide plus an anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam, per IDSA and local microbiology.
Treat raised ICP while awaiting surgery; a neurosurgeon may tap the shunt reservoir as a temporising measure.
Correct coagulopathy before any device revision or new insertion, per local protocol.

definitive.text: Mechanical shunt failure: urgent shunt revision, or a temporary EVD in the deteriorating patient.
Infected shunt: remove the infected hardware, place an external drain, treat with antibiotics, and re-implant when CSF cultures are clear.
Blocked EVD: neurosurgical assessment, with aseptic flushing or replacement per local policy.
EVD-associated ventriculitis: replace or remove the drain where possible, and tailor antibiotics to culture.

escalate.text: A shunted patient with symptoms belongs in a neurosurgical centre. If transfer is needed, it is an emergency transfer.
Paediatric shunt patients: involve the paediatric neurosurgical team early; deterioration can be abrupt.
Microbiology input for every device infection, including duration of therapy and timing of re-implantation.

notes: Ventricles in a long-standing shunt can stay small even when the shunt has failed. Treat the patient, not the scan.
An EVD is a pressure-controlled drain. If the reference point or the chamber height is wrong, the drainage is wrong.
Most shunt infections declare within months of the last operation and come from skin organisms at the time of surgery.
